title.narrative: ICRC operations by the Brasilia (regional) Delegation(2025 Unaudited)

description.narrative: The ICRC has been operating in Argentina since the 1970s. Our work focuses on the identification of unidentified Argentine soldiers buried at Darwin Cemetery in the Falkland/Malvinas Islands. We also foster adoption and promotion of International Humanitarian Law (IHL) in the armed forces and in the academic communities, and support the National Committee for the Implementation of IHL. In addition, we cooperate with the Argentine Red Cross. Brazil is the headquarters of the ICRC’s regional delegation for Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Paraguay and Uruguay. Our work in Brazil focuses on responding to and promoting responses from political leaders to the humanitarian needs of people affected by armed violence. The ICRC fosters IHL and raises awareness of the suffering which family members of missing persons go through, among political leaders and the public. We also provide support and training in the identification of the remains of missing persons. The ICRC has an office in São Paulo, and seeks the support of Brazilians, whether for donations or joining the ICRC, and cooperates with the Brazilian Red Cross (CVB). In Chile, the ICRC works toward mitigating the humanitarian consequences of violence in the south of the country. Our local staff visit prisoners in order to ensure that they are treated with dignity, encourage implementation of IHL by the armed forces and support implementation of International Human Rights Law (IHRL) and the humanitarian principles applicable to the law enforcement community. In addition, we cooperate with the Chilean Red Cross. The ICRC fosters income generation and enhanced nutrition in communities affected by violence, and works towards providing essential services such as water. We also deliver first aid training and provide psychosocial support to these communities. Our local ICRC staff visit prisoners in order to ensure that they are treated with dignity and foster implementation of IHL and IHRL by the civilian and military authorities and national security forces. We also collaborate with the Paraguayan Red Cross and the International Federation to respond quickly and effectively to the needs of victims affected by violence or other emergencies. The ICRC encourages implementation of the IHL in the armed forces and supports the work of the National Committee for the Implementation of IHL.
